nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show nanoflower-like morphology composed of interconnected 2D nanosheets for Se-CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1b) of Se-CoP show the nanoflower-like morphology composed of interconnected 2D nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms nanoflower-like morphology of interconnected 2D nanosheets for Se-CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1b) of Se-CoP show the nanoflower-like morphology composed of interconnected 2D nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows average nanosheet thicknesses of 4.4±0.1 nm for Se-CoP and 4.5±0.1 nm for CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average thicknesses of Se-CoP and CoP nanosheets are ca. 4.4±0.1 and 4.5±0.1 nm, respectively, as evidenced by the atomic force microscopy (AFM) images (Figures 1c, S2, and S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Se-CoP possesses BET specific surface area of 21 m² g⁻¹ and highly mesoporous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Se-CoP possesses a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area of 21 m² g⁻¹ and a highly mesoporous structure (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping proves uniform distribution of Co, P, and Se elements in Se-CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images (Figure 1d) prove that the presence and uniform distribution of Co, P, and Se elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES verifies Co, P, and Se contents in Se-CoP as 26.6, 25.8, and 14.3 wt%, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) and element analysis verify that the Co, P, and Se elements in Se-CoP are 26.6, 25.8, and 14.3 wt%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM identifies lattice fringes of 0.249 and 0.187 nm corresponding to (111) and (211) planes of orthorhombic CoP in Se-CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 1e) clearly identifies the lattice fringes of 0.249 and 0.187 nm, corresponding to the (111) and (211) crystal planes of orthorhombic CoP (JCPDS No. 29-0497).

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing lattice fringes
High-resolution TEM image showing lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD patterns confirm orthorhombic CoP crystal phase for both Se-CoP and CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns (Figure 1f) of both Se-CoP and CoP further confirm this crystal phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA indicates Se-CoP exhibits excellent thermal stability in inert atmosphere.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) indicates that Se-CoP exhibits excellent thermal stability in an inert atmosphere (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Co 2p peaks at 778.7/792.9 eV (Co-P, +0.4 eV shift vs CoP), P 2p at 129.3/130.2 eV (P-Co), 137.7 eV (Se-P), Se 3d at 55.4/56.2 eV (Co-Se) confirm Se incorporation into Se-CoP lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the high-resolution Co 2p spectra of Se-CoP and CoP (Figures S6a and S7a), the binding energies of Co 2p₃/₂ and Co 2p₁/₂ exhibit characteristic peaks at 778.7 and 792.9 eV, attributing to the Co-P bond. Notably, compared with CoP, the binding energy of Co 2p for Se-CoP displays positive shifts of 0.4 eV... For the high-resolution P 2p spectrum of Se-CoP (Figure S6b), the binding energies of P2p₃/₂ and P2p₁/₂ exhibit characteristic peaks at 129.3 and 130.2 eV... Additionally, a new peak at 137.7 eV is induced by the selenium doping, corresponding to the Se-P bond. As for Se 3d spectrum of Se-CoP (Figure S6c), the two peaks fitted at 55.4 and 56.2 eV originate from the binding energies of Se 3d₅/₂ and Se 3d₃/₂ in Co-Se bond, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Non-operando Co K-edge XANES shows higher valence states of Co in Se-CoP compared to CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, compared with CoP, the binding energy of Co 2p for Se-CoP displays positive shifts of 0.4 eV (Figure 1g), being consistent with the results of non-operando Co K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra (Figure S8), which indicates higher valence states of Co after the introduction of Se atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Non-operando Co K-edge FT-EXAFS reveals surface oxidation effects consistent with XPS Co-O species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be further revealed by the non-operando Co K-edge Fourier transform (FT) extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra (Figure S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-HER HRTEM of Se-CoP shows lattice spacing of 0.264 nm ((200) Co(OH)₂ planes) in intermediate state and 0.198 nm ((002) Co planes) in final state with cluster-level metallic Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images display a lattice spacing of ca. 0.264 nm that belongs to (200) crystal planes of Co(OH)₂, indicating the transformation of CoP to Co(OH)₂ (Figures 3a,b and S27)... another lattice spacing of 0.198 nm is observed in a very small size range of the HRTEM image (Figure 3c), which belong to the (002) crystal plane of Co (JCPDS No. 05-0727).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando PXRD during HER shows characteristic (100), (002), (102) peaks of trigonal Co(OH)₂ (JCPDS 30-0443) with higher peak intensities for Se-CoP vs CoP as potential decreases to -0.55 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando PXRD patterns (Figures 3d and S30) exhibit the characteristic peaks of (100), (002), and (102) crystal planes, which belongs to trigonal Co(OH)₂ (JCPDS No. 30-0443). Note that, as the reduction potentials increased from 0 to -0.55 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), Se-CoP exhibits higher peak intensities of Co(OH)₂ phase compared with CoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-HER SAED shows clear Co(OH)₂ diffraction spots for Se-CoP but none for CoP, indicating higher crystallinity of Se-CoP derived Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Also, clear Co(OH)₂ diffraction spots can be observed in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) image of Se-CoP (Figure 3e), while no obvious spot on that of CoP (Figure 3f).

properties.description: Selected Area Electron Diffraction pattern with (100) and (102) planes

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Co K-edge XAS during HER shows absorption edge shift to higher energies (increasing Co valence), faster structural transformation in Se-CoP (Co-P disappears at 0 V vs RHE, Co-O CN=2.46→3.04, Co-O distance shrinks 2.010→1.955 Å), and more stable Co nanoclusters vs CoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We further conducted operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) measurements on Se-CoP and CoP during HER... The Co K-edge XANES spectra of Se-CoP and CoP (Figures 3h and S31) indicate that the absorption edge is gradually shifted to higher energies as the applied potentials increased from open circuit voltage (OCV) to -0.3 V versus RHE... For Se-CoP, the Co-P scattering path disappeared and the coordination number (CN) of Co-O path raises to 2.46±0.45 when the potential applied. Further increase the potential, the CN of Co-O path raises to 3.04±0.21 at -0.3 V versus RHE, meanwhile, the bond length of Co-O shrinks from 2.010 to 1.955 Å.
